settings.key_insight: The question isn't just 'how long does a yak chew last' — it's 'how long does it last for MY dog.' Weight, jaw strength, chew style, and age all matter. Here's how to actually calculate it.
settings.article_body:
"How long will this last?" is the first question almost every customer asks. It's also the hardest to answer honestly, because the real answer is: it depends.

I've seen a 30lb dog finish a Large in 45 minutes. I've seen a 70lb dog work a Medium for three days. The difference isn't just size — it's chew style, jaw strength, and how the dog approaches the chew.

The four factors that determine chew duration

1. Weight

This is the starting point. Our size guide is built around weight ranges: Small (under 25lb), Medium (25–50lb), Large (50–85lb), XL (85lb+). But weight is just the baseline.

2. Chew style

Power-chewers — dogs who bite down hard and fast — go through chews 2–3x faster than methodical gnawers. If your dog attacks a chew like it owes them money, size up.

3. Age

Puppies (under 1 year) have softer teeth and tend to chew more gently. Senior dogs (7+) often chew more slowly. Both groups typically get longer sessions from the same size chew.

4. Session length

We recommend 20–30 minute supervised sessions, then putting the chew away. This extends the total lifespan of the chew significantly and prevents overconsumption.

Real duration data from our customers

Based on thousands of logged sessions in our My Dog dashboard:

  • Medium chew, 35lb methodical chewer: 3–5 sessions (6–10 hours total)
  • Large chew, 60lb power-chewer: 2–3 sessions (40–90 minutes total)
  • XL chew, 90lb+ dog: 3–6 sessions (2–5 hours total)

These are medians — your dog will vary. That's why we built the My Dog dashboard: log your first session and we'll predict your reorder timing.

The puff trick adds one more session

When the chew gets down to a 1-inch nub, microwave it for 45–60 seconds. It puffs up into a crunchy, airy treat. Most dogs treat this as a separate reward — it's not just the end of the chew, it's a bonus.

Don't skip this step. It's one of the things that makes yak chews genuinely better value than they look at first glance.
